approval_statement: I approve the Gohr D4 label-shuffle protocol under near_chance_baseline_gated_v4. The primary endpoint is exact-binomial TOST for near-chance equivalence of each shuffled-label fit around chance accuracy 0.5, using margin 0.005 and band [0.495, 0.505] at alpha 0.05. Overall SUPPORTED additionally requires every intact-label baseline fit to have a one-sided 95% exact lower confidence bound strictly above 0.90. The chance margin and baseline-adequacy floor are protocol-owner-selected practical tolerances, not values prescribed by the overarching methodology, the D4 planning note or Gohr's paper. The paired McNemar comparison is secondary and non-gating, with effect_threshold 0.01. The protocol uses five planned replicates, training/validation/test sizes of 10000000/1000000/1000000 and 200 epochs. Label shuffling is a blunt control and does not rule out all forms of leakage; targeted generation-order and label-leakage audits are outside this D4 protocol. The thresholds were not selected using the September historical D4 outcome.
data_examined_before_approval: Before approval, I reviewed the proposed v4 decision rules, numerical thresholds, source-provenance record, rationale, approval sheet and reported offline validation results. I reviewed rationale section 0.5 on the baseline-adequacy threshold and its design-only operating-characteristic calculations, section 0.7 on the chance margin and its design-only operating-characteristic calculations, and section 4 on partition overlap and prior measurements. Section 4 reports zero duplicate rows, zero cross-partition overlap, and zero label conflicts for the D0 Gohr production instance, which is a different dataset. Those D0 measurements establish nothing about the new D4 partitions. The historical September 2026 D4 result was reported as EFFECT_DETECTED. Its per-replicate arrays were unavailable, were not inspected, and were not used to select the new thresholds. No v4 preflight, calibration, or production run has occurred, and no v4 outcome data was examined before approval.

overarching_methodology.role: The overarching audit methodology. It governs this protocol's general statistical rules, listed under sections_applied.

3.9.4 (confidence interval for every primary result, including distinguishing accuracy)
3.9.6 (hypotheses fixed before results; post hoc analyses exploratory)
3.9.8 and 3.9.9 Rule III (failure to reject a null is not evidence of equivalence)
overarching_methodology.does_not_define: D4 label shuffling, the near-chance criterion, the blunt-control caveat, or any numerical margin. Its Controlled Perturbation stage (3.6.4 Stage 4) lists regeneration with independent seeds, deduplication, changed partitioning, class balancing and alternative sampling.

methodology_source.not_derived_from: The September 2026 EFFECT_DETECTED result. Neither the hypotheses, the margin nor the baseline floor was chosen from it.

relation_to_prior_evidence: The September 2026 D4 run (audit/dataset/evidence/d4/, config_hash b41cf02a..., outcome EFFECT_DETECTED) is historical evidence under an earlier procedure: last-epoch evaluation, no hash-bound selection, unverified label reuse, and rule conservative_two_sided_v1. Its outcome refers to a paired difference from baseline, not to near-chance accuracy or baseline adequacy. Its status (EFFECT_DETECTED) is known. Its per-replicate arrays and partitions are not on disk; they were not inspected as new data, and they were never audited for overlap. It was not used to choose the margin, the baseline floor, or any rule. Drafts v2 (directional_iut_v2) and v3 (near_chance_tost_v3) were never approved or run.
question: Can Gohr's 5-round Speck32/64 training pipeline produce above-chance held-out accuracy when the original feature/label correspondence of its training data is destroyed by permuting the training labels? Expected diagnostic result: near-chance accuracy.

hypothesis.shuffled_H0: Non-equivalence: for at least one perturbed fit r, p_r <= 0.5 - chance_margin or p_r >= 0.5 + chance_margin.
hypothesis.shuffled_H1: Near-chance equivalence: for every perturbed fit r = 1..k, 0.5 - chance_margin < p_r < 0.5 + chance_margin.
hypothesis.shuffled_departure_claim: Some perturbed fit departs from the band (p_r > U or p_r < L). Established only by the Bonferroni departure tests.
hypothesis.baseline_H0: Inadequacy not excluded: for at least one intact-label baseline fit r, q_r <= baseline_adequacy_threshold.
hypothesis.baseline_H1: Adequacy: for every baseline fit r = 1..k, q_r > baseline_adequacy_threshold.
hypothesis.baseline_inadequacy_claim: Some baseline fit is below the floor (q_r < t). Established only by the Bonferroni inadequacy tests.
hypothesis.supporting_H0: For at least one replicate the perturbed model is not less accurate than its paired baseline.
hypothesis.supporting_H1: For every replicate the perturbed model is less accurate than its paired baseline on the same test rows, by at least effect_threshold.
hypothesis.direction: Shuffled: equivalence (two one-sided tests), with departure on either side. Baseline: one-sided, accuracy above the floor. Supporting: one-sided, perturbed worse than baseline.
hypothesis.not_a_substitute: A reduction relative to baseline never establishes near-chance accuracy or baseline adequacy. For example, 0.70 is far below a 0.929 baseline and far from chance.

estimand: p_r and q_r are the accuracies, at threshold 0.5, of the reloaded selected models of perturbed fit r and intact-label baseline fit r, over the test-generating distribution, conditional on each model. They are estimated by X_r / n on the fixed test partition. Sampling: the test partition is one speck.make_train_data(n, 5) call, which draws each label as an independent os.urandom bit and each row's key and plaintexts afresh, so rows are i.i.d. and class counts are not fixed. The partition is generated independently of training and reaches only predict(). Hence, given a model, its correctness indicators are i.i.d. Bernoulli and X_r ~ Binomial(n, p_r) exactly; no stratified procedure is needed. Supporting: delta_r = (b_r - c_r) / n on the same rows. All fits share one test sample. Their outcomes are dependent and are never pooled as if there were k*n independent examples; every claim is per fit, combined by IUT or Bonferroni, neither of which needs independence.

conditions.baseline: Model fit on the original training partition (features, labels).
conditions.perturbed: Model fit on the same features with labels permuted by LabelShufflePerturbation using the replicate's audit RNG stream.
conditions.pairing: Both fits of a replicate use the same model seed, the same validation partition and the same training protocol; only the training labels differ. Both are evaluated on the same test examples.

perturbation.name: label_shuffle
perturbation.construction: indices = rng.permutation(n_train) as little-endian int64, with rng = default_rng(SeedSequence(audit_seed).spawn(replicates)[r-1]); perturbed_labels[i] = train_labels[indices[i]]; features unchanged.
perturbation.definition_check: LabelShufflePerturbation.verify: features byte-identical; labels same length, dtype and label multiset.
perturbation.persistence: Only the permutation indices are persisted per replicate. Before any reuse they must be a bijection of range(n_train) with dtype <i8 and length n_train, match their SHA-256, equal the permutation the audit seed regenerates, and their sidecar must bind them to the training-data and training-label digests, condition (perturbed), replicate, model seed, audit seed and perturbation name. The perturbed labels are re-derived from them and checked against the recorded perturbed-data digest.

fixed_design.source: Carried unchanged from the existing D4 run configuration (audit/dataset/evidence/d4/run_manifest.json) and Gohr's published training procedure; approved as a whole by the top-level approval.

dataset.randomness: os.urandom (not seedable); partitions are generated once at preflight and persisted, never regenerated
dataset.split: three independent make_train_data calls: train, validation, test
dataset.input_encoding_check: validated from the actual arrays at preflight and again before run and verify

model_selection.reload: The selected epoch checkpoint is reloaded from disk and is the only model used for test predictions.

seeds.model_seed: per replicate, SeedSequence(audit_seed).spawn(replicates)[r-1].generate_state(1)[0]; identical for the two conditions of a replicate

bootstrap.role: descriptive only; not used by any decision

fixed_design.test_isolation: The test partition is given only to predict() of selected models; adapters are constructed without test arrays and see only its digest. No test statistic is computed before all fits of all replicates are complete.

procedure.estimand: per perturbed fit: test accuracy p_r of the reloaded selected model, conditional on that model
procedure.sampling_model: test rows i.i.d. from make_train_data (labels independent urandom bits, class counts not fixed); X_r ~ Binomial(n, p_r) given the model

primary_endpoint.chance_reference_assumptions: 0.5 is the exact accuracy of any predictor independent of the label when labels are fair coin flips, independent of the features, as speck.make_train_data documents (os.urandom bits). The observed test class counts are recorded in the certificate and not tested here; label balance is D3's subject.
primary_endpoint.rule: Per fit r: EQUIVALENT if P(X>=x|L) < alpha and P(X<=x|U) < alpha. ABOVE_BAND if P(X>=x|U) < alpha/(2k). BELOW_BAND if P(X<=x|L) < alpha/(2k). Otherwise INDETERMINATE. Joint: SUPPORTED iff all k are EQUIVALENT; NOT_SUPPORTED iff any is ABOVE_BAND or BELOW_BAND; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE; NOT_COMPLETED if any fit is missing.
primary_endpoint.reported_per_fit: correct count, n, accuracy, both TOST p-values, the 1-2*alpha Clopper-Pearson interval, both departure p-values and the 1-alpha/k Clopper-Pearson interval, state

procedure.estimand: per replicate: delta_r = acc(perturbed_r) - acc(baseline_r) = (b - c) / n on the same test rows
procedure.discordance: b = baseline wrong & perturbed right; c = baseline right & perturbed wrong

supporting_endpoint.rule: Established iff, for every replicate, P(B<=b | b+c, 1/2) < alpha and delta_r <= -effect_threshold. When b+c = 0 the p-value is 1, so the endpoint is not established.
supporting_endpoint.reported_per_replicate: b, c, delta_r, one- and two-sided exact McNemar p-values, conditional exact interval for delta_r (given b+c)

procedure.estimand: per intact-label baseline fit: test accuracy q_r of the reloaded selected model, conditional on that model
procedure.sampling_model: same test rows and binomial model as the near-chance endpoint

baseline_adequacy_endpoint.rule: Per baseline fit r: ADEQUATE iff P(X>=x | t) < alpha, i.e. the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound is strictly greater than t. INADEQUATE iff P(X<=x | t) < alpha/k, i.e. the one-sided 1-alpha/k upper bound is strictly below t. Otherwise INDETERMINATE. Gate: PASSED iff all k are ADEQUATE; FAILED iff any is INADEQUATE; otherwise INDETERMINATE; NOT_COMPLETED if any fit is missing.
baseline_adequacy_endpoint.reported_per_fit: correct count, n, accuracy, both p-values, the one-sided lower bound (level alpha), the one-sided upper bound (level alpha/k), state
baseline_adequacy_endpoint.no_selective_reruns: The k baseline fits are those of the registered seed plan. No fit is re-run, replaced or excluded after its accuracy is seen; a crash resumes only through the verified recovery, and integrity failures end the run as NOT_COMPLETED.

overall_rule.SUPPORTED: otherwise, near-chance endpoint SUPPORTED and baseline-adequacy gate PASSED

fixed_design.class_conditional_diagnostics: Per fit, true-negative rate (label 0) and true-positive rate (label 1) with their counts are reported descriptively only. They are not confirmatory and never change any outcome.

comparability_to_published_pipeline.published_benchmark: Gohr (CRYPTO 2019), as cited by the protocol owner: 5-round Speck32/64, input difference 0x0040/0000, test accuracy 0.929 on 10^6 test samples, basic pipeline with 10^7 training samples, 10^6 validation samples and 200 epochs. The paper was not available to the agent offline; these figures are as cited.
matches_repository_code: train_5_rounds.py (Gohr upload, commit fba2fd7): train_speck_distinguisher(200, num_rounds=5, depth=10); this protocol uses depth 10 and 200 epochs
train_nets.make_resnet with reg_param 1e-5; compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mse'); batch size 5000; LearningRateScheduler(cyclic_lr(10, 0.002, 0.0001))
data: speck.make_train_data(10^7, 5) for training and (10^6, 5) for validation; the test partition is a separate (10^6, 5) call
selection: Gohr keeps ModelCheckpoint(monitor='val_loss', save_best_only=True); this protocol selects the argmin-val_loss committed epoch, earliest on ties, and reloads it
evaluation: accuracy at threshold 0.5 on fresh data
differences: shuffle=False in fit (Gohr uses the Keras default shuffle=True), chosen for deterministic data order; the rows are i.i.d., but the effect on final accuracy has not been measured
seeded initialisation per replicate (Gohr's runs were unseeded)
TensorFlow/Keras 2.15 runtime rather than the original Keras/TF versions
train_nets.py carries a local seed-control modification (commit 6062a31)
comparability_to_published_pipeline.consequence: The pipeline is close to, but not identical to, the published one, so 0.929 is a reference level, not a guaranteed reproduction. The baseline floor is set below it as an explicit practical tolerance; it is not validated by the paper.

decision_rule.rationale: Overall SUPPORTED requires near-chance equivalence of every shuffled fit and adequacy of every intact-label baseline fit. The paired comparison is secondary and non-gating. Paired-only rules (directional_iut_v2, conservative_two_sided_v1) cannot establish near-chance accuracy, and v3 had no baseline gate, so this runner refuses them. Their code stays in the engine to reproduce historical evidence.

chance_margin.rationale: chance_margin fixes the near-chance band [0.5 - delta, 0.5 + delta]; the candidate 0.005 gives [0.495, 0.505], with chance reference 0.5 and alpha 0.05. It is a separate quantity from effect_threshold, which is a minimum paired difference from baseline. It is an explicit practical design choice of the protocol owner. Neither the overarching methodology PDF nor the D4 planning note (section F) prescribes a numerical D4 margin, and Gohr's paper does not either. What the band means for this diagnostic: a label-shuffled fit counts as 'near chance' if its population test accuracy is established to be within half a percentage point of 0.5. That is at most about 1.2% of the published 5-round signal (0.929 - 0.5 = 0.429). So the control asks whether shuffling removes essentially all of the pipeline's advantage, not whether it removes every conceivable trace. A residual advantage larger than 0.005 surviving the shuffle is treated as a practically relevant leak; one inside the band is not ruled out by D4 and remains the province of the targeted leakage screens (section E). The test-set size does not set the margin. n = 10^6 determines precision and the operating characteristics, not what is scientifically acceptable, and the margin was not narrowed because a narrower one would still be powered. The margin must not be selected or altered using any new D4 result, and the historical September D4 result does not determine it. Design-only operating characteristics (n_test = 10^6, alpha = 0.05, k = 5; table below): at 0.005, P(a fit is not EQUIVALENT | p_r = 0.5) = 6.5e-17, so P(all five EQUIVALENT) >= 1 - 3.3e-16 by the union bound; a fit with true accuracy 0.5025 is declared equivalent with probability 0.9996; the size at the band edge is <= 0.05. Any reproducible advantage is exploitable in principle given enough data, so the band does not mean 'cryptanalytically worthless'.

operating_characteristics.inputs: n_test = 1000000, alpha = 0.05, k = 5; exact binomial; computed with the engine functions; no D4 outcome data used
columns: union lower bound P(all 5 EQUIVALENT | p=0.5)

baseline_adequacy_threshold.rationale: The intact-label baseline-adequacy floor t. A near-chance result for the shuffled models is informative only if the same pipeline, with intact labels, does distinguish the classes. Each of the k registered baseline fits is ADEQUATE only if its one-sided 95% exact lower confidence bound on test accuracy is strictly greater than t. The gate passes only if all k are adequate. Candidate 0.90: a proposed reproduction-adequacy threshold. It is not prescribed by Gohr or by the audit methodology. The published 5-round benchmark is 0.929 on 10^6 test samples, as cited by the protocol owner. The floor sits 2.9 percentage points below it, as an explicit practical tolerance for differences between this pipeline and the published one: shuffle=False, seeded initialisation, and the TF 2.15 runtime (fixed_design.comparability_to_published_pipeline), and for seed-to-seed training variation. That variation is NOT measured by the paper's test-set uncertainty: at n = 10^6 the binomial standard error at 0.929 is about 0.00026, which describes one model's test sample, not how much accuracy varies between training runs. No repository evidence measures the seed-to-seed spread of this pipeline, so the 2.9-point tolerance is a judgment, not an estimate. Operating characteristics (design only): with n = 10^6 and alpha = 0.05, a fit is ADEQUATE iff it has at least 900494 correct predictions and INADEQUATE iff at most 899301. P(ADEQUATE | q = 0.929) = 1, P(ADEQUATE | q = 0.902) = 1.000, P(ADEQUATE | q = 0.901) = 0.955, P(ADEQUATE | q = 0.90) = 0.0499 (the size). It was not chosen from the September D4 result or from any new D4 baseline. Weak baselines are never re-run or excluded after their accuracy is seen.

paired_endpoint_role.rationale: The paired McNemar comparison (one-sided exact, perturbed worse, effect_threshold 0.01, IUT over replicates) is reported as a secondary, supporting endpoint and never changes the outcome. It is secondary because the D4 question concerns the shuffled condition: a shuffled model can be much worse than its baseline and still far from chance. The concern that a co-primary role used to address (a baseline that itself shows no signal) is now handled directly by the baseline-adequacy gate, which tests absolute baseline accuracy rather than a difference. The certificate marks the endpoint secondary_non_gating. Citing it as an additional confirmatory claim would raise the familywise error to <= 2*alpha; it is supporting evidence only.

alpha.rationale: alpha = 0.05 is the level of each TOST one-sided test (each fit's equivalence is a 90% exact interval inside the band), the level of each baseline adequacy test (one-sided 95% lower bound), the level of the intersection-union claims (all shuffled fits equivalent; all baselines adequate; both together), and the familywise level of the Bonferroni departure (alpha/(2k) per one-sided test) and inadequacy (alpha/k per test) families. It is also the level of the secondary paired IUT. Carried from the existing configuration.

effect_threshold.rationale: Supporting endpoint only: the minimum paired accuracy reduction delta_r <= -effect_threshold, as a fraction (0.01 = one percentage point). It is an operational practical-relevance threshold carried from the existing configuration, not a validated margin. It is never used as the near-chance margin.

replicates.rationale: Carried from the existing configuration. Each replicate is 2 x 200 epochs on 10^7 rows; k=5 makes the replicate-level criteria about reproducibility across seeds, not a population estimate.

sample_sizes.rationale: Carried from the existing configuration and Gohr's 5-round setting.

epochs.rationale: Carried from the existing configuration and Gohr's published 5-round training length.

partition_overlap_policy.rationale: Measured at preflight on the actual persisted partitions, before any training. Features are 64-bit rows from os.urandom-keyed encryptions, so expected accidental cross-partition collisions are about n_a*n_b/2^64 (about 5e-7 for train-test), and any shared row signals a generation defect. train-test and validation-test sharing would let fitted or selection-used rows into evaluation; train-validation sharing would bias checkpoint selection. A refusal ends this protocol; the partitions are kept and not regenerated, deduplicated or altered, and any new dataset needs a documented, prospective protocol amendment.

within_partition_duplicates_policy.rationale: A duplicate inside one partition does not cross the fit/selection/evaluation boundary; it is recorded in the evidence with its label-conflict count. It is also astronomically unlikely here, so a non-zero count should be reported as an anomaly in the write-up.

label_conflict_reporting.rationale: Feature-row overlap and label agreement are checked separately: within each partition, distinct feature rows seen with more than one label; across partitions, shared rows whose labels differ. Under the recommended overlap policy any cross-partition row already refuses, so label conflicts add information but not a separate gate.

failure_handling.rationale: No replicate is ever excluded or replaced. A crash may be resumed only through the adapter's verified recovery (uncommitted epochs quarantined and retrained, all retries recorded); any integrity refusal stops the run, and the outcome is then NOT_COMPLETED (no certificate; verify exits 5), never as a result on fewer replicates. Stopping rule: the run ends when all k replicates finish; there is no interim look at test statistics.

calibration.rationale: Every confirmatory test is exact: binomial tails for the TOST, departure and baseline tests, and the conditional binomial for McNemar. Their levels hold given i.i.d. test rows from the generator, independent of training, which holds by the generator's construction (estimand). No simulation calibration is needed for the error guarantees. test_d4_near_chance.py checks the software against exact rational-arithmetic references and exact level computations on small enumerated cases. That is software validation, not scientific calibration.

outcomes.overall_d4_outcome: One of SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, BASELINE_INADEQUATE, INCONCLUSIVE, NOT_COMPLETED, by fixed_design.overall_rule. Only SUPPORTED is a successful control; INCONCLUSIVE, BASELINE_INADEQUATE and NOT_COMPLETED are never reported as passes. Integrity verification success is reported separately and is not scientific success.
outcomes.baseline_adequacy_gate: PASSED, FAILED (a baseline demonstrably below the floor), INDETERMINATE (adequacy not established, inadequacy not established) or NOT_COMPLETED
reported: per shuffled fit: correct count, n, accuracy, TOST p-values, 90% Clopper-Pearson interval, departure p-values and interval, state
per baseline fit: correct count, n, accuracy, adequacy and inadequacy p-values, one-sided bounds, state
per replicate: b, c, delta_r, exact McNemar p-values (one- and two-sided), conditional exact interval for delta_r
per fit, descriptive: true-negative and true-positive rates with counts
descriptive: mean and SD of delta_r, percentile bootstrap CI of mean delta_r; selected epoch and val_loss per fit; test class counts

provenance_requirements: preflight.json: preregistration SHA-256 anchor and commit, source identity, partition files with SHA-256, canonical partition digests, input-encoding check, overlap audit and policy outcome
per fit: hash-chained epoch records, state.json, selected_checkpoint.json with every epoch checkpoint digest and the train/validation/evaluation digests
per replicate: perturbation sidecar binding the perturbed labels to the source training digest
result/: certificate and run manifest written once, exclusively; manifest binds certificate SHA-256, preflight SHA-256, source identity and run id
verify stage: recomputes every p-value and the decision, re-verifies every fit chain and checkpoint, every perturbation and every partition file
per fit: raw test predictions of the reloaded selected model (fits/predictions/replicate_NN_<condition>.npy), with SHA-256, dtype and shape in the certificate

verify stage: recounts every fit's correct count, class-conditional counts and (b, c) from those predictions and the preflight-bound test labels, then recomputes every endpoint statistic and the outcome. verify --rerun-models also reloads every selected checkpoint (SHA-256 checked) and requires its thresholded test predictions to equal the persisted ones. Fits are never re-trained (see certificate methodology.verifiability).
scope_and_limitations: Label shuffling is a blunt control: it removes genuine signal and label-correlated artifacts together. A near-chance result does not show that no leakage of any form exists.
Inference is conditional on each fitted model and the shared test sample. 'All k' is a statement about these k training seeds, not a population estimate over seeds.
A non-chance result shows that the pipeline extracts label information without the original correspondence. It does not identify the mechanism, which needs the targeted checks below.
TensorFlow training is not bitwise deterministic; seeds fix initialization and data order, not every floating-point result.
Hash chains detect corruption and substitution relative to digests held elsewhere; they are not signatures.
The dataset depends on os.urandom; the claim is about this persisted instance and the generator, not a re-derivable seed.
The baseline floor and the near-chance margin are registered practical tolerances; neither is derived from the PDF, the planning notes or the paper.

items: targeted generation-order leakage check (e.g. label predictable from row position or generation batch)
targeted label-leakage check (label recoverable from features or metadata by construction, not by cryptographic signal)
complementary_audits_not_in_scope.note: No outcome of this protocol may be reported as covering these checks.
